question: What percent of Americans will oppose the Iran War on the eve of Election Day 2026?

calls.reasoning: Silver Bulletin tracker shows opposition at 55% (support 36%) as of Oct 22-23, 2026, down from 60% at the start of October. Status quo is that value persisting through Nov 2, about 10 days out. Model: random walk around 55, with a small hedge between momentum (support is ticking up and the administration is reportedly holding off on escalation before the midterms) and mean reversion toward the summer-to-early-fall level of ~56-60%, so net drift is about zero. Fresh polls show little sign of a sharp move: AP-NORC (Oct 22) has strong desire to end the war, and Fox shows 56% opposing back in July. The tails cover new escalation or gas-price shocks. No human prediction market was found (Manifold's Iran civil-war market does not match).
calls.dossier:
- Silver Bulletin tracker (natesilver.net, updated Oct 22-23, 2026): support 36%, oppose 55%. The tracker says support rose from 32% at the start of October to 36%, and opposition fell from 60% to 55% over the same period.
- Silver Bulletin, Oct 16 update: support 35%, up from an all-time low of 32%. The last poll showing net-positive support was in April 2026.
- When tracking began (Nate Silver Substack note, date unclear, early in the war): 39.5% support, 52.1% oppose, with opposition 'inching up'.
- Fox News poll, Jul 17-20, 2026: 56% oppose US military action against Iran (40% strongly); 66% disapprove of Trump's handling of Iran, a record.
- Pew, Oct 8, 2026: war 'remains deeply unpopular'; many expect it to last months.
- AP-NORC, Oct 22: about 7 in 10 registered voters want the next Congress to prioritize ending the war. One poll, about 65% disapprove / 33% approve of Trump's handling.
- UMass Lowell/YouGov, Oct 2026: reports 71% on an opposition-related question (wording differs from the tracker's support/oppose framing).
- Silver Bulletin context: the administration appears to be delaying major military action until after the midterms and trying to bring gas and diesel prices down. More oil is moving through Hormuz despite attacks, and gas prices remain elevated.
- Status quo: the Nov 2 value equals the latest value (~55%).
- Resolves off the Silver Bulletin CSV ('Get the data') value for Nov 2, 2026, not the chart (CSV takes precedence). If Nov 2 is missing, the closest earlier date is used. The CSV may carry decimals.
- Event window: single-date reading, Nov 2, 2026. As of Oct 25, about 10 days remain.
- Searched for but not found: the CSV's daily series and decimal values (paywalled/not accessible), any prediction market on this tracker, and any scheduled major escalation.
calls.reference_class: Changes over 10-day windows in poll-aggregate averages of opinion on salient ongoing wars/policies (e.g., Silver Bulletin/538 issue averages); 10-day changes typically within +/-2-3 pts

calls.reasoning: Silver Bulletin average: 55% oppose / 36% support as of Oct 22-23, down from 60% at the start of October. With ~8-10 days until the Nov 2 reading, the status quo is ~55. Downward momentum (pre-midterm restraint on military action, more oil through Hormuz) is partly offset by persistently high opposition in individual polls and by escalation risk, so the median sits slightly below 55. No human market matches this question (the Manifold Iran civil-war market is unrelated).
calls.reconciliation: All runs agree on the factual anchor: 55% opposition on Oct 23, falling from 60%. The disputes were all judgment calls: how much the downward momentum persists vs. reverts, and how wide the tails should be. I gave the momentum modest weight because smoothed averages tend to keep trending and its causes remain in place, so the median is 54.8. The decimal precision of the CSV could not be checked and is absorbed into the width. I see no concrete mechanism for an upside escape before Nov 2, so only the downside escape gets mass (small).
